title: Project Midnight Caprice
subtitle: 1974 Chevrolet Caprice Classic Restomod Convertible
narrative: Project Midnight Caprice transforms a 1974 Chevrolet Caprice Classic convertible into an aggressive twin-turbo restomod, featuring twin VSR 70/70 billet T4 turbochargers on an LS3 408 stroker engine, Morimoto bi-LED projector headlights, custom stainless script badges, and an integrated roll bar with dove grey interior.
Views of the finished car are AI concepts; the photographs are the car as it stands.

specifications.Lighting: Morimoto Bi-LED Projector Headlights / BTF-Lighting FCOB Red LED Strips
specifications.Exterior: Aerofoil Streamline Tubing Grille / Custom 'Midnight Caprice' Stainless Badges
specifications.Interior: Dove Grey Interior / Custom Integrated Roll Bar
specifications.Suspension: Modified SLA front and triangulated 4-link rear, using the factory frame mount locations with the axle mounts adjusted. Air bags at all four corners: the car lays frame and still clears a driveway
specifications.Steering: Rack and pinion, a little tighter than most
specifications.Structure: Suspension loads front and rear transfer into an inner stiffening structure: an underdash hoop tied to truss work low in the door openings, up to the overhead roll bar, with down bars hidden inside the body panels. Only the roll bar is plainly visible. It is not a cage, because that aesthetic does not go with a convertible; the truss takes the hinge out of the car. The truss work is not finished yet; much of the rest is
specifications.Tires & Wheels: C8 Corvette take-offs, run for break-in: Michelin Pilot Sport 4 S, 245/35ZR19 (89Y) front and 305/30ZR20 (99Y) rear, GM TPC spec, on black C8 split-five-spoke wheels with machined rim edges and crossed-flags caps. The intent is to go as large as the car will take once it is running; these roll the car through break-in, expendable if they get injured. The wheel style is liked; it may stay, or it may change.

builderNotes: Crossroads, Nov 2026: Kraftsman has given up on the project; the car transfers to Omar at Double-O Garage. Before the transfer Kraftsman promised to finish two things: the bumper fitting (done) and the headlight enclosures (still to complete). After the transfer, the next-steps conversation with Omar sets the punch list. Candidates so far: the grille, my design, four panels via SendCutSend; complete the downdraft diverter from the scoop and re-fit the filters beside the radiator. Funnies is the then-and-now set: the June 30, 2023 Helen Mirren composite (found photo, pasted figure, Google Bard era) beside its Nov 27, 2026 remake (one generated photograph, face-referenced and realism-graded, the lettering re-set by hand both times): what the models learned in three years.

title: Project ScapeGoat
subtitle: 1968 Pontiac Street & Strip Outlaw Drag Car
narrative: Project ScapeGoat transforms a 1968 Pontiac into a full street-and-strip outlaw drag car, built as the high-horsepower outlaw counterpart to its factory-bodied 'Body Brother' restomod.

The build started in October 2026 at the chassis. The central X-member was started on Oct 14 and mocked up on Oct 21. The driveshaft retainer hoops came fresh off the new bender on Oct 23, and the center shaft retainer cage was under construction by Nov 7, its plate plasma-cut on Nov 11. The rear frame is still unmodified: the 1-inch notch comes later, cut clear of the frame's CON-VIN stamp zone, and the wide rear tires get covered by moving the rear fenders' outer sheet metal out, not flares. The drivetrain is decided (built 6.2L L94, T56 Magnum, Ford 9-inch) and the hunt for the engine and gearbox is live. The car's Alpine Blue is confirmed by original paint still on the body; its VIN is still unknown, narrowed to the 242378Z1346xx block.

specifications.Drivetrain: 4.0-inch Aluminum Driveshaft / Weld ProStar 15x15 Rear Wheels
specifications.Chassis: Custom central X-member (in fabrication); 1-inch frame rail notch planned, clear of the CON-VIN stamp zone

builderNotes: Shop punchlist: 1) Finish center shaft retainer cage including lower plate. 2) Weld in retainer cage and X-member. 3) Notch and box the frame. 4) Weld in new coilover mounts from BMR Suspension. 5) Grind and sand frame; prep for paint and rust inhibition. 6) Define the suspension installation. 7) IDEA on file (2026-11-24): woven-wire mesh door panels, per the reference photo (Projects/ScapeGoat mesh door panel reference.jpg, unlinked): the framed mesh panel Scot photographed on a green T-bucket's door, a workable treatment for ScapeGoat's door panels, likely a better idea than the previous one. Decide at the door stage.
